purpose: Record one bounded OpenMC transport observation and a separate deterministic free-memory refusal check for PERF-041.

workload.known_lower_bound_definition: 8 bytes times (mesh bins + ordinary scalar responses). This is a structural lower bound, not a peak-RSS estimate.

Close other programs and run it again, or, if the job is known to be small, lower the cap with FARIS_MEMORY_CAP_MB.; known workload lower bound 0.00 GiB (1152 mesh-bin scalars; 46 ordinary response scalars; 30 batches; 0 triangles; 297970 request/input bytes recorded for context but not counted as resident); solver/runtime overhead is unknown, hard cap 0.25 GiB

refusal_check.interpretation: The extreme reserve deterministically exercised refusal before solver launch; it is not a realistic free-memory threshold.

limitations: This is one 30000-history smoke run, not the default-size study peak measurement.
The known scalar-result lower bound is 9584 bytes while sampled job peak is 542359552 bytes; unknown solver and native-library working memory dominates and remains unmodeled.
The Linux process-group peak is sampled every 50 ms and can miss brief peaks; the cgroup high-water mark measures a broader scope and is recorded separately.
The refusal check used an intentionally extreme reserve and does not validate a realistic host-memory boundary.
A cgroup-constrained smoke run is not a stress test; no OOM or maximum-workload behavior was tested.
